result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another, from other species, and from the Earth itself.

This shift would dissolve the roots of greed, conflict, and exploitation, because you can’t harm what you recognize as part of yourself. It wouldn’t erase difference or individuality, but it would make cooperation as instinctive as breathing. Systems built on domination (capitalism, nationalism, speciesism) would collapse not through force, but because they’d feel as absurd as a hand trying to strangle the body it belongs to.

The ripple effects would be vast: economies designed for mutual thriving, justice as a reflex, technology wielded like a tool instead of a weapon, and a relationship with the living world based on reciprocity rather than extraction.

But the real magic? It wouldn’t require new laws or revolutions—just the quiet, irreversible knowing that *we are the world changing itself*. The rest would follow.
